transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

It is actually normal for a Beko washer-dryer to use water during a drying programme. Most models use a trickle of cold water to cool down the condenser, which turns the steam from your clothes back into liquid so it can be pumped away. This explains why you hear water running and draining. Please tell me: 1. Was the load small enough for drying (usually about half the washing capacity)? 2.
Thank you. The message seems to have cut off after your first question. As for that one, I put in a small load of dry-ish clothes, so I believe it was within the limit. What was your second question?

My apologies for the cut-off. My second question was: once the drying programme finished, were the clothes actually dry or did they come out damp? If they are damp, we need to check if the machine drained properly during the spin phase before it started heating.
The clothes came out dry, yes. The machine isn't damp or leaking anywhere either, so it all seems to work - I just wanted to be sure that the water noise is normal for a machine only two months old.

Yes, that is completely normal for a Beko washer-dryer. As I mentioned, the machine uses a trickle of cold water during drying to cool down the condenser and turn steam back into liquid so it can be pumped away. Since your clothes came out dry and there are no leaks, the appliance is working exactly as designed. You don't need to do anything further.
